$comment: The Actions block's anatomy, case by case: the stored node in, the exact markup out.
Hand-authored and read by BOTH renderers' suites — the React `view`
(bundle-src/test/actions-anatomy.test.tsx) and the Chameleon template
(src/.../tests/test_view_actions_block_view.py). The two renderers must emit
the same anatomy element for element, because one scope-wrapped stylesheet
dresses both surfaces; this file is what holds them to a FIXED list rather
than to whichever renderer landed first.
`html` is the markup INSIDE the host's block wrapper, on the PUBLIC surface.
The wrapper's own `block block-actions has--block-width--<w>` stamp is the
host's and is not our output.
No whitespace between elements: the Plate editable computes
`white-space: pre-wrap`, so an inter-element newline becomes a real line box.
JSX drops it by construction; the server template strips its indentation.
Both suites compare EXACTLY, up to attribute order (each sorts attributes
before comparing), and again as the SKELETON — every attribute but `class`
removed, text kept — which is the cross-renderer contract. The two renderers
emit identical attributes here: the catalog's `url` is the absolute URL Plone
computed for the request, and both emit it as-is.
The editor surface is `html` with every `href` dropped (the canvas-safety
rule), and nothing else changed.
`catalog` in `data` is the DERIVED key the server's serializer injects: every
offered category mapped to its `{id, title, url}` rows. A node without one is
a node the server has never serialized, and both renderers draw the empty root.

cases.name: empty
cases.note: Exactly one element: the root with the DEFAULT category and its label. Containers are never emitted empty, and the canvas's notices live outside the root.

cases.name: category-without-catalog
cases.note: A category chosen on a node the server has never serialized: the root still carries the EFFECTIVE category, so the author can recognise the block, and nothing else renders.

cases.name: site-actions
cases.note: The reference case: the stock site actions, one list item per row, each carrying its per-action modifier.
cases.html:
• Site Map
  • Accessibility
  • Contact

cases.name: title-and-list
cases.note: The optional heading sits above the list, inside the root, as an h2 — a block that never enters the outline is invisible to anyone navigating by heading.
cases.html:
More

  • Site Map

cases.name: title-only
cases.note: A heading with nothing under it still renders: it is the author's own content, and the list is conditional on its own.

cases.name: title-not-a-string
cases.note: Nothing is required and nothing is trusted: a title that is not a string is an absent title.

cases.name: picks-the-stored-category-out-of-the-whole-catalog
cases.note: The catalog carries EVERY offered category; only the stored one renders. That is what makes switching the category in the sidebar instant.
cases.html: • Home

cases.name: object-buttons
cases.note: Every offered category is spelled the same way; the label is the table's.
cases.html:
• Delete
  • Rename

cases.name: unknown-category-falls-back
cases.note: A category the block does not offer renders the DEFAULT one, from the same catalog, so a hand-authored node still shows something the author recognises.
cases.html: • Site Map

cases.name: category-missing-from-catalog
cases.note: A serialized node whose stored category has no rows — anonymous asking for object buttons, say — is the empty root. The canvas says why; the public page says nothing.

cases.name: catalog-not-an-object
cases.note: A hand-authored catalog of the wrong shape is no catalog at all.

cases.name: row-without-title-dropped
cases.note: A link with no text is worse than an absent one; the row renders nothing.
cases.html: • Contact

cases.name: row-without-url-dropped
cases.note: Symmetric with the title rule: a link that goes nowhere renders nothing.
cases.html: • Contact

cases.name: unscreened-url-dropped
cases.note: The catalog travels inside a JSON node anyone with API access can hand-author, so a URL is screened like typed input: a scheme outside the allowlist is treated exactly as no URL.
cases.html:
• Mail
  • Relative

cases.name: unsafe-id-gets-no-modifier
cases.note: An id that is not a slug gets no per-action class rather than an escaped one; the base class always stays.

cases.name: rows-of-the-wrong-shape-skipped
cases.note: A row that is not an object is skipped, and whitespace around a title or URL is trimmed.
